tests.title: Unit 7: Bank Reconciliation Statement – Practice Test 1

questions.question_text: The balance as per cash book is Rs 50,000 (Dr). Cheques issued but not yet presented are Rs 8,000 and cheques deposited but not yet collected are Rs 5,000. The balance as per pass book is:
The pass book shows a balance of Rs 72,000 (credit). Cheques deposited but not credited Rs 6,000 and cheques issued but not presented Rs 9,000. The cash book balance is:
Bank charges of Rs 250 debited by the bank in the pass book, but not yet entered in the cash book. The cash book balance (Dr Rs 12,000) should be adjusted to:
A cheque for Rs 3,000 was deposited and dishonoured. The cash book still shows it as collected. To reconcile, the cash book balance (Dr Rs 20,000) will be:
Interest on deposits of Rs 1,200 credited by the bank but not in the cash book. A cash book debit balance of Rs 30,000 will be updated to:
Direct deposit by a customer Rs 4,500 appears in the pass book only. The effect on the cash book balance is to:
A standing instruction to pay insurance premium Rs 2,000 appears only in the pass book. The cash book needs:
The cash book shows an overdraft of Rs 15,000. Cheques issued not presented Rs 4,000 and cheques deposited not credited Rs 2,000. Balance as per pass book (overdraft) is:
The balance as per the pass book is overdraft Rs 20,000. Cheques issued not yet presented Rs 6,000. Overdraft as per cash book is:
questions.explanation: Unpresented cheques mean the cash book shows more overdraft.

questions.question_text: A bank reconciliation statement is prepared in order to:
options: Verify the arithmetical accuracy of the trial balance of the firm
Explain the difference between the cash book and pass book balances
Calculate the net profit of the business for the whole year
Record the cash sales and cash purchases made by the business

questions.question_text: The bank reconciliation statement is prepared by:
options: The bank, from its records for each customer
The business, from its cash book and the pass book
The auditor, at the end of the year
The Reserve Bank of India, every quarter

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a timing difference?
options: Cheques issued but not yet presented
Bank charges not recorded in the cash book
questions.explanation: The cash book needs no correction for it.

questions.question_text: Which of these requires a correction in the cash book?
options: Cheques issued but not yet presented
Cheques issued but not yet encashed
Bank charges shown in the pass book only
Cheques deposited but not yet credited

questions.question_text: Which of the following does not need an adjustment in the cash book?
options: Direct payment by a customer into the bank
Interest on overdraft debited by the bank
Dividend collected directly by the bank
questions.explanation: Timing items only affect the pass book.

questions.question_text: The cash book balance is Rs 18,500 (Dr). Items: bank charges Rs 150 (pass book only); interest Rs 700 credited (pass book only); cheque dishonoured Rs 1,000 (cash book not updated). Corrected cash book balance is:
The pass book shows Rs 40,000. Cheques issued not presented Rs 5,000; cheques deposited not credited Rs 3,000. The cash book balance would be:

The pass book shows Rs 40,000 (credit). Cheques deposited but not credited are Rs 3,000 and cheques issued but not presented Rs 5,000. Interest Rs 500 and bank charges Rs 200 appear in the pass book only. The correct (adjusted) cash book balance is:
questions.explanation: Interest and charges are already in the pass book; 40,000 + 3,000 − 5,000.

questions.question_text: A cheque for Rs 5,000 issued to a supplier has not been presented, and the cash book was not otherwise in error. As compared with the cash book, the pass book balance (favourable) is:
questions.explanation: The bank has not yet debited the account.

questions.question_text: A debit balance in the pass book means the:
options: Customer has money in the bank

questions.question_text: A credit balance as per the pass book indicates:
Cheques deposited by the firm but not yet credited by the bank appear in the reconciliation because the:
options: Cash book and pass book are both silent on the cheques
Cash book has already been debited but the pass book has not
Bank has credited the cheques twice by mistake
Pass book has already been credited but the cash book has not

questions.question_text: The bank statement shows a credit of Rs 3,200 for a bill collected on behalf of the firm, not yet in the cash book. The cash book balance must be:
options: Increased by debiting the bank column with Rs 3,200
Decreased by crediting the bank column with Rs 3,200
Increased by crediting the bank column with Rs 3,200
Left alone, as bank collections are not entered in it

questions.question_text: Bank charges Rs 100 appear in both the cash book and the pass book. Treatment in BRS is:
A cheque issued for Rs 7,500 was debited by the bank as Rs 5,700. As compared with the correct balance, the pass book balance (favourable) is:
A cheque of Rs 2,000 deposited was entered twice in the cash book. The cash book balance is overstated by:

tests.title: Unit 7: Bank Reconciliation Statement – Practice Test 2

questions.question_text: If bank balance as per cash book is Rs 3,000 (Dr) and a debit of Rs 600 for a returned cheque appears only in the pass book, the corrected cash book balance is:
If the cash book shows Rs 6,400 overdraft and interest on overdraft Rs 400 in the pass book only, the overdraft in the cash book after adjustment is:
Dividend of Rs 900 received directly by the bank and credited in the pass book. Cash book (overdraft Rs 5,000) after adjustment shows overdraft of:
Out of a deposit of three cheques totalling Rs 12,000, one for Rs 4,000 is not credited by the bank by the end of month. The bank column in the cash book includes:
The date of recording a cheque in the cash book is when it is:
The pass book is a copy of the account in the:
questions.explanation: Bank's statement of the customer's account.

questions.question_text: BRS is NOT part of:
The BRS starting with the cash book balance (Dr) is: Cash book Rs 10,000 + cheques issued not presented Rs 3,000 − cheques deposited not credited Rs 2,000. The balance as per pass book is:
While preparing the BRS from the cash book (overdraft), a cheque deposited but not credited is:
questions.explanation: Overdraft as per pass book is more.

questions.question_text: A cheque for Rs 1,400 given to a supplier is recorded in the cash book but not yet presented. Pass book balance (credit) will be:
options: Lower than the cash book by Rs 1,400
Higher than the cash book by Rs 1,400

questions.question_text: A cheque for Rs 800 was deposited and the bank did not credit it until next month. The pass book balance is:
options: Higher than the cash book by Rs 800
Lower than the cash book by Rs 800

questions.question_text: The pass book shows Rs 55,000 (credit). Cheques issued but not presented are Rs 9,000, cheques deposited but not credited Rs 11,000, and interest Rs 500 appears in the pass book only. The adjusted cash book balance is:
questions.explanation: 55,000 + 11,000 − 9,000; interest is already in the pass book.

questions.question_text: The bank deducted Rs 120 as a cheque book fee. The cash book entry should be:
options: Dr Cash column; Cr Bank column
Dr Bank charges account; Cr Bank column
No entry, since it is a timing difference
Dr Bank column; Cr Bank charges account
questions.explanation: An expense paid by the bank.

questions.question_text: Cheque deposited in the bank on 31 March, credited by the bank on 3 April. On 31 March the pass book balance is:
A cheque issued on 28 March for Rs 3,000 presented on 5 April. At 31 March the pass book balance is:
Which of the following would reduce the pass book balance relative to the cash book?
Which of the following would increase the cash book balance relative to the pass book?
questions.explanation: Debits to cash book not recorded.

questions.question_text: Which of the following adjustments reduce the cash book balance?
The firm finds that the cash book wrongly recorded a deposit of Rs 7,000 as Rs 700. The cash book balance:
options: Needs to be increased by Rs 6,300
Needs to be decreased by Rs 6,300

questions.question_text: Cash book overdraft of Rs 9,000. Bank erroneously credited another customer's cheque of Rs 1,200 in the account. The pass book overdraft is:
Updated cash book balance is used for the:
The adjusted cash book balance is Rs 58,000. The pass book balance is Rs 62,000, and the only reconciling item is cheques issued but not yet presented. These cheques total:
The firm and the bank both wrongly recorded a deposit for the same amount. In the BRS:
options: The amount is deducted from the cash book balance
The amount is added to the pass book balance
No adjustment is needed, as both records agree
The amount is deducted twice from the pass book

questions.question_text: Preparing the BRS starting with the pass book balance is helpful when:
options: The bank has made an error in the pass book entries
The cash book balance is to be derived from the pass book
Both the balances are already known and agree with each other
The pass book has been lost or not received from the bank

questions.question_text: The proprietor drew Rs 4,000 by cheque, but the cash book credit shows Rs 40,000. As compared with the correct balance, the cash book balance is:

tests.title: Unit 7: Bank Reconciliation Statement – Practice Test 3

questions.question_text: The BRS shows that the balance as per the pass book is higher than the cash book by Rs 3,000. This could be due to:
questions.explanation: Pass book still includes the amount.

questions.question_text: The pass book is lower than the cash book by Rs 3,000. This could be due to:
The cash book balance and pass book balance are both Rs 12,000. The reconciliation may still contain items because:
options: Pass book is always right and the cash book wrong
Errors are impossible in either record
Bank charges are always recorded in the cash book
Several items may offset each other exactly

questions.question_text: Which of these is not a reason for a difference between cash book and pass book?
options: Wrong totalling in the sales book

questions.question_text: After reconciliation the bank balance is Rs 25,000. The pass book shows Rs 5,000 overdraft, and the only items are deposits not credited. The deposits not credited are:
Bank pass book shows a credit balance Rs 10,000. A cheque of Rs 1,500 issued by the firm has not been presented. A cheque of Rs 800 deposited not yet credited. Updated cash book balance is:
If a cheque deposited earlier is returned unpaid, the cash book entry is:
A cheque of Rs 5,000 issued to a supplier is dishonoured for lack of funds and the bank also charges a penalty. The firm's cash book:
options: Must be closed and a fresh cash book opened
Must be adjusted for the penalty debited in the pass book
Must be increased by the amount of the cheque
Needs no adjustment as the cheque was not paid

questions.question_text: If the bank and the firm both record a cheque issued but it was entered in the pass book in the next month, the item is classed as:
The pass book on 1 April opened with a credit balance of Rs 7,000. Receipts Rs 20,000, payments Rs 15,000. Closing balance is:
A cheque for Rs 3,600 collected by the bank on behalf of the firm appears in the pass book but not in the cash book. The firm's cash book balance:
The bank pays a bill payable Rs 6,000 on the firm's instruction. The firm has not entered it in the cash book. The cash book balance should be:
A cheque of Rs 800 was entered on the debit side of the cash book instead of the credit side. The cash book balance is overstated by:
A cheque of Rs 1,000 issued last month was not presented then. It is presented this month. In this month's BRS the cheque:
options: Is no longer a reconciling item
Is added to the cash book balance
Is deducted from the pass book balance
Remains a reconciling item as before

questions.question_text: Besides reconciling balances, a BRS also helps in:
options: Valuing the closing stock lying in the godown
Calculating the profit of the business for the year
Detecting frauds and errors in the cash and bank records
Finding the capital of the proprietor at the year end

questions.question_text: A bank statement shows a closing balance Rs 40,000. Uncredited deposits Rs 8,000, unpresented cheques Rs 5,000. Adjusted bank balance is:
The unadjusted cash book balance is Rs 44,000 and bank charges of Rs 1,000 are not yet entered. The adjusted cash book balance is:
The unadjusted cash book balance is Rs 20,000. Receipt of Rs 5,000 from a debtor recorded in the cash book as Rs 500. Corrected balance is:
The cash book balance is Rs 16,000 and the pass book balance Rs 17,000. Cheques issued not presented Rs 2,000 and deposits not credited Rs 1,000. The pass book figure is correct if:
options: It cannot be checked from the figures given

questions.question_text: A dividend of Rs 1,500 collected by the bank for the firm is credited in the pass book only. The cash book balance must be:
A firm deposited a cheque of Rs 5,000 on 30 June, but the bank credited it on 2 July. The BRS prepared on 30 June treats it as:
options: A cheque issued but not yet presented
A cheque deposited but not yet credited
A bank charge recorded in the pass book only
An error made by the bank in its records

questions.question_text: A cheque issued on 28 June is dated 5 July but entered in the cash book on 28 June. The BRS on 30 June shows it as:
options: A cheque issued but not yet presented
An error in the cash book to be corrected
Interest credited by the bank in the pass book
A bank charge recorded in the pass book only

questions.question_text: The pass book shows an overdraft of Rs 48,000 against a limit of Rs 50,000, and cheques of Rs 4,000 issued have not been presented. When they are presented the overdraft will be:
Which of the following transactions does NOT appear in the pass book?
options: Cash sales kept in the firm's till
Bank charges levied on the account

questions.question_text: An amount debited by the bank in error Rs 900 will be:
options: Added to the pass book balance

tests.title: Unit 7: Bank Reconciliation Statement – Practice Test 4

questions.question_text: The BRS to find the cash book balance from the pass book includes starting with:
BRS on 30 April: Cash book overdraft Rs 6,000; cheques issued not presented Rs 2,500; deposits not credited Rs 1,500. The pass book overdraft is:
If total of deposits not credited is Rs 10,000, cheques issued not presented Rs 10,000 and the cash book is Rs 50,000, the pass book balance is:
The bank debits Rs 1,500 as interest on a loan, and the firm has not yet recorded it. The cash book needs:
options: A reversal of the entry already made by the firm
No entry, as it is a timing difference only
A credit entry of Rs 1,500 in the bank column
A debit entry of Rs 1,500 in the bank column

questions.question_text: The cash book is Rs 4,000 lower than the pass book. The reason could be:
options: Bank charges of Rs 4,000 debited in the pass book
Cheques of Rs 4,000 deposited but not yet credited
Cheques of Rs 4,000 issued but not yet presented
Dishonour of a customer's cheque of Rs 4,000
questions.explanation: The pass book is higher by that amount.

questions.question_text: The bank credits Rs 2,500 by credit transfer from a debtor, not yet in the cash book. The cash book:
options: Is debited in the bank column with Rs 2,500
Is left unaffected, as it is a timing difference
Is closed and balanced again at the month end
Is credited in the bank column with Rs 2,500

questions.question_text: Debit entry Rs 600 in the pass book for the proprietor's insurance premium is, in the cash book, entered as:
Rs 10,000 credited in the pass book by mistake belongs to another customer. In the BRS, the pass book needs:
Which one is a valid reason for an overdraft in the cash book but credit in the pass book?
questions.explanation: Cash book shows a lower balance.

questions.question_text: The pass book shows a credit balance of Rs 20,000, and the cash book shows an overdraft of Rs 3,000. The only reconciling item is cheques issued but not presented, of:
Which of these statements is correct?
options: A BRS can be prepared at any date
A BRS must be prepared daily

questions.question_text: Rs 15,000 cheque issued appears in the pass book as Rs 15,000 but in the cash book as Rs 1,500. The cash book balance needs:
A trade creditor was paid Rs 4,000 by direct bank transfer on the firm's order. In the cash book this is recorded by:
options: No entry, since it is only a memorandum matter
Debit to the bank column and credit to the creditor
Credit to the bank column and debit to the creditor
Debit to the cash column and credit to the creditor

questions.question_text: The pass book shows Rs 25,000 (credit). Cheques issued but not presented Rs 8,000. Bank charges of Rs 3,000 and interest of Rs 2,000 appear in the pass book only. The adjusted cash book balance is:
questions.explanation: 25,000 − 8,000; charges and interest are already in the pass book.

questions.question_text: The accountant's bank column in the cash book is credited when:
The pass book shows an overdraft of Rs 18,000. Cheques deposited but not credited are Rs 2,000. The overdraft as per the cash book is:
If the bank credits Rs 3,000 as interest which relates to another customer, the correct entry in the BRS is:
options: Add Rs 3,000 to the pass book
Deduct Rs 3,000 from the pass book
Add Rs 3,000 to the cash book

questions.question_text: A bank reconciliation statement is not necessary if:
options: The two balances agree and there are no reconciling items
The firm issues a large number of cheques each month
The firm is a large concern with several bank accounts
The cash book shows a debit balance with the bank

questions.question_text: A cheque deposited at the end of one month is credited by the bank in the next month. In the first month's BRS it is:
options: Written off as an error in the books of the firm
Not a reconciling item, as both records show it
A reconciling item, deducted from the cash book to reach the pass book
A reconciling item, added to the cash book to reach the pass book
questions.explanation: Not yet credited by the bank.

questions.question_text: The cash book balance after adjusting it with all items not yet recorded is called:
Bank charges of Rs 220 were deducted twice by the bank in error. The pass book balance as compared to the correct balance is:
Cheque for Rs 6,500 from X was returned unpaid by the bank. The firm also pays Rs 100 as noting charges. Cash book should show a reduction of:
A cheque issued for Rs 2,000 is lost and stopped. The cash book will:
The discount column of a three-column cash book:
options: Is posted to the pass book by the banker every month
Is deducted from the bank column when the BRS is prepared
Is added to the bank column when the BRS is prepared
Is a memorandum column and does not affect the bank balance

questions.question_text: After bank reconciliation, the amount to be reported in the balance sheet as 'cash at bank' is:
